adventure.title: Walk with Dinosaurs at Dinosaur Ridge
adventure.description: The hogback outside Morrison preserves hundreds of real dinosaur tracks and bones in the rock where they were found — walk the ridge road and put your hand where a brontosaur stepped.
adventure.bonus: Count the tracks on the main slab and photograph the biggest print next to your hand.

adventure.title: Fall Through Reality at Meow Wolf Convergence Station
adventure.description: Four floors of interdimensional transit station built into a highway interchange — Denver's Meow Wolf rewards the curious with hidden doors, secret narratives, and rooms that should not exist.
adventure.bonus: Find a passage nobody around you has noticed and go through it first.

adventure.title: Dawn Hike into Waterton Canyon
adventure.description: The wide canyon road along the South Platte is bighorn sheep country, and first light is when the herds come down to the river — day-use land, so the early alarm is the whole strategy.
adventure.bonus: Hike the first three miles with your headlamp off — moonlight or bust.

adventure.title: Paraglide from Lookout Mountain in Golden
adventure.description: Lookout Mountain is the Front Range's premier training and tandem paragliding launch, where you step off a ridge and float over Buffalo Bill's grave with the Denver skyline spread below you.
adventure.bonus: Ask your pilot to let you steer during the flight — actually take the toggles and hold a turn for 10 seconds.

adventure.title: Summit Quandary Peak — Colorado 14er
adventure.description: Quandary Peak is the most-climbed 14er in Colorado for good reason: the East Ridge route is direct, the views of the Tenmile Range are staggering, and you earn real bragging rights at 14,265 feet.
adventure.bonus: Start before 5 a.m. and summit before 10 a.m. — then call someone from the top who said you wouldn't make it.

adventure.title: Ski Loveland Basin on a Powder Day
adventure.description: Loveland is the closest true ski resort to Denver and its exposure to the Continental Divide means it catches snow before anyone else — locals know this; tourists drive past it to Breckenridge.
adventure.bonus: Ski one run on Chair 9 with your phone in your pocket — no GoPro, no Strava, just the mountain.

adventure.title: Whitewater Raft Clear Creek Canyon from Idaho Springs
adventure.description: Clear Creek delivers some of the most accessible Class III–IV whitewater in Colorado, and the canyon walls make it feel genuinely remote despite being 45 minutes from downtown Denver.
adventure.bonus: Volunteer to sit in the front of the raft for the Class IV Notorious rapid — no swapping spots mid-canyon.

adventure.title: Scramble the First and Second Flatirons
adventure.description: The classic Boulder scramble climbs the tilted sandstone of the First and Second Flatirons — no ropes, full attention, and a summit view that reframes the entire Front Range.
adventure.bonus: Sign the summit register and write one honest sentence about why you actually came out here today.

adventure.title: Sunrise at Red Rocks Amphitheatre
adventure.description: Red Rocks hits different at dawn when the 400-foot sandstone formations glow orange and the only people here are trail runners and a handful of people who set an alarm worth setting.
adventure.bonus: Run every single row of seats — top to bottom, bottom to top — before the sun clears the ridge.

adventure.title: Mountain Bike the Apex Park Enchanted Forest Trail
adventure.description: Apex Park in Golden is the closest legitimate singletrack to Denver and the Enchanted Forest loop delivers punchy climbs and fast technical descents in under an hour.
adventure.bonus: Clean the rock garden section at the bottom of Sluicebox without dabbing — one clean run counts.

adventure.title: Kayak Confluence Park on Cherry Creek
adventure.description: Where Cherry Creek meets the South Platte River in the heart of Denver, kayakers and stand-up paddlers navigate real current within walking distance of downtown bars.
adventure.bonus: Paddle through the Confluence whitewater channel without putting a hand down — no bracing allowed.

adventure.title: Hike the Mount Falcon Park Summit Trail
adventure.description: The ruins of a never-finished presidential summer retreat sit at the top of this Jefferson County open space trail with unobstructed Front Range views that make every step worth it.
adventure.bonus: Touch the Walker Home ruins and eat your lunch sitting on the foundation stones.

foodie.title: A Scoop at Bonnie Brae Ice Cream
foodie.description: This corner parlor has hand-made its ice cream since 1986, and the summer-evening line down the block is a Denver ritual — cinnamon is the sleeper order.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever flavor the person in front of you got — no vetoes.

foodie.title: Cliff Divers and Sopapillas at Casa Bonita
foodie.description: The pink palace of Lakewood — reborn under new owners who actually fixed the food — still runs cliff divers off a 30-foot indoor waterfall while you eat. There is nowhere else like it on earth.
foodie.bonus: Raise the little flag for more sopapillas at least twice — tradition demands it.

foodie.title: Saturday Morning at the South Pearl Street Farmers Market
foodie.description: From May through November, South Pearl turns into Denver's best open-air pantry with Hazel Dell mushrooms, Palisade peaches, and tamale vendors that make the whole street smell incredible.
foodie.bonus: Spend exactly $20 on ingredients and commit to cooking dinner from whatever you buy before you leave the block.

foodie.title: Lamb at the Buckhorn Exchange
foodie.description: Denver's oldest restaurant — liquor license #1, opened 1893 — serves elk, quail, and Rocky Mountain oysters under 500 mounted animals in a dining room that makes every meal feel historic.
foodie.bonus: Order the Rocky Mountain Oysters as a starter — no explanation to your tablemates allowed until after they've tried one.

foodie.title: Late-Night Ramen at Uncle, LoHi
foodie.description: Uncle's spicy chicken ramen is a deep, glossy obsession that turns a cold Denver night into something worth staying out for — counter seats reward solo missions.
foodie.bonus: Add the seasoned egg, bamboo, and extra chashu — then slurp loudly and unapologetically.

foodie.title: Counter Seat at Sushi Den
foodie.description: The Kizaki brothers have been flying fish in daily from Japanese markets since 1984, and eating at the sushi bar in South Pearl is as close to Tsukiji as Denver gets.
foodie.bonus: Skip the menu entirely and ask the itamae for an omakase selection — whatever he's excited about tonight.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Fruition Restaurant
foodie.description: Alex Seidel's flagship on East 6th Avenue has quietly been one of the most precise farm-to-table kitchens in the mountain west for nearly two decades.
foodie.bonus: Ask the server which dish came from Seidel's own Fruition Farm this week and order it, whatever it is.

foodie.title: Green Chile at El Taco de Mexico
foodie.description: The James Beard America's Classic counter on Santa Fe Drive has ladled Denver's benchmark green chile over stuffed sopapillas since 1985 — stools, formica, perfection.
foodie.bonus: Ask for extra green chile on the side and see how many bowls of chips you can justify before your entree arrives.

foodie.title: Breakfast at Lucile's Creole Café
foodie.description: This Boulder-born institution serves the best beignets and eggs Sardou on the Front Range from a converted Victorian house that always has a line worth joining.
foodie.bonus: Order the blackened catfish instead of whatever you planned and finish every drop of the café au lait.

foodie.title: Brunch at Snooze AM Eatery on Ballpark
foodie.description: The original Snooze location on Ballpark's edge still runs the longest lines on weekend mornings because the rotating pancake flights and benedict variations are genuinely worth the wait.
foodie.bonus: Order one pancake you'd never normally pick — let the server choose for you.

foodie.title: Green Chile Smothered Burrito at My Brother's Bar
foodie.description: Denver's oldest bar — pouring since 1873, no signage, Kerouac and Cassady's old haunt — and the jalapeño cream cheese burger ordered off the wall menu is the city's most storied lunch.
foodie.bonus: Order a Coors from the tap, sit at the bar, and strike up a conversation with whoever's next to you — no phones during the drink.

foodie.title: Dinner at Mizuna
foodie.description: Frank Bonanno's intimate Capitol Hill restaurant has been Denver's best special-occasion table since 2001, running a French-American menu that trusts its ingredients enough to leave them mostly alone.
foodie.bonus: Order the tasting menu and tell the server to pick the wine pairings — no menu-browsing allowed.

active.title: Volleyball on the Wash Park Courts
active.description: Washington Park is Denver's unofficial volleyball capital — on summer weekends the grass courts stretch the length of the park and pickup games absorb anyone standing too close.
active.bonus: Rotate into a game of strangers and stay for three sets minimum.

active.title: Backcountry Snowshoe at St. Mary's Glacier
active.description: Colorado's most accessible year-round glacier sits an hour from Denver and rewards snowshoers with a frozen alpine lake and a legitimate sense of wilderness.
active.bonus: Glissade down the glacier's main slope on your rain jacket — then hike back up and do it again.

active.title: Yoga on the Rocks at Red Rocks
active.description: On summer Saturday mornings the amphitheater itself becomes the studio — a thousand mats between the monoliths, sun cresting the plains mid-flow. Tickets go fast.
active.bonus: Hold tree pose facing the formations for 60 seconds on each leg without wobbling.

active.title: Ice Skate at Evergreen Lake
active.description: Colorado's most scenic winter skating rink sits on a frozen mountain lake at 7,000 feet, surrounded by pine forest with the Continental Divide in the distance.
active.bonus: Skate the full perimeter of the lake without stopping — no rails, no breaks.

active.title: Sunset Ride on the Bear Creek Trail from Morrison
active.description: This winding canyon bike path follows Bear Creek through red-walled cliffs into the foothills, hitting its golden hour right when the rock face lights up amber.
active.bonus: Ride all the way to Lair o' the Bear Park and dip your hands in the creek before turning back.

active.title: Tube Clear Creek Through Golden
active.description: Rent a tube, put in above town, and ride glacier-cold Clear Creek right through downtown Golden — locals stack laps all summer and dry off on the grass at Parfet Park.
active.bonus: Hold position in the main wave for 10 full seconds without getting pushed out — hands-free.

active.title: Climb Green Mountain in Lakewood
active.description: This relentless grind up Green Mountain's south ridge rewards you with a 360-degree panorama that stretches from Pikes Peak to Rocky Mountain National Park.
active.bonus: Summit without headphones in — pay attention to every breath and name one thing you see in each cardinal direction at the top.

active.title: Disc Golf at Paco Sanchez Park
active.description: Denver's flagship disc golf course throws over the hills west of the river with skyline views on the back nine — free, walkable from the light rail, and busy every golden hour.
active.bonus: Ace basket 9 — or buy everyone in your group a beer if you can't par it.

active.title: Lap the Sloan's Lake Park Loop
active.description: Denver's biggest in-city lake wraps you in mountain views and serious runner energy on a flat 2.6-mile loop that locals own every morning.
active.bonus: Run the full loop without stopping, then do 20 push-ups at the west shore overlook facing the Rockies.

active.title: Bouldering at the Morrison Boulderfield
active.description: The south-facing sandstone blocks below Morrison are the Front Range's classic winter bouldering circuit — pull on real rock twenty minutes from downtown while the high country freezes.
active.bonus: Send a V3 or harder without using your knees once — no cheater knees allowed.

active.title: Skate the Denver Skate Park at Confluence Park
active.description: The city's flagship concrete skate park sits at the convergence of the Platte River and Cherry Creek and draws a genuine cross-section of Denver — from toddlers on push bikes to grown men landing rails.
active.bonus: Drop in on the biggest bowl you're afraid of — once is enough, but once is required.

active.title: Morning Ride on the High Line Canal Trail
active.description: The 71-mile historic irrigation ditch trail cuts through Denver's southeastern suburbs under a canopy of century-old cottonwoods that make you forget the city exists entirely.
active.bonus: Ride at least 15 miles without stopping to check your phone — just move and look at the trees.

active.title: Run the Cherry Creek Trail
active.description: Denver's creek-side artery runs protected below street level from Confluence Park deep into the southeast — pick a distance, follow the water, and let the underpasses do the pacing.
active.bonus: Run your first mile without music or podcasts — just the creek and whatever's in your head.

social.title: Summer Night at Lakeside Amusement Park
social.description: Open since 1908, Lakeside is a working time capsule — a wooden Cyclone coaster, hand-painted signs, and vintage neon reflecting off the lake for the price of a modern movie ticket.
social.bonus: Ride the Cyclone in the front car after dark.

social.title: Two-Step Night at the Grizzly Rose
social.description: Denver's legendary country dancehall has run boots across its 5,000-square-foot floor since 1989 — free dance lessons early, live bands late, and a mechanical bull with no mercy.
social.bonus: Take the free lesson, then use it with a stranger — and yes, the bull counts for bonus bragging rights.

social.title: Comedy Show at Comedy Works Downtown
social.description: Since 1981 this basement club has launched careers and hosted legends — grab a two-drink minimum seat and sit close enough to get called out.
social.bonus: Sit in the first three rows — front row if it's open — and don't flinch when the comic makes eye contact.

social.title: Sunday Afternoon at Breckenridge Brewery's Farmhouse in Littleton
social.description: This sprawling outdoor farmhouse campus with cornhole, fire pits, and a working farm has become Denver's best suburban escape for easy afternoons that turn into long evenings.
social.bonus: Challenge a group of strangers to cornhole — loser buys the next round.

social.title: Denver Broncos Game at Empower Field at Mile High
social.description: Mile High's energy on gameday is a full-body Colorado experience — 76,000 people at altitude in orange and navy, absolutely unhinged for three hours.
social.bonus: Start a chant in your section — if it spreads three rows in either direction, you win the day.

social.title: Afternoon Pint at the Wynkoop Brewing Company
social.description: Colorado's original brewpub — opened in 1988 by a future governor — anchors LoDo with legendary billiards, honest pub food, and house-brewed beers that earned the whole state its craft reputation.
social.bonus: Win a game of pool against a stranger and buy them a beer if you lose.

social.title: Live Jazz at Dazzle
social.description: Denver's premier jazz club — now at the Denver Performing Arts Complex — books world-class musicians in a room small enough to feel every note.
social.bonus: Go alone, sit at the bar, and talk to the person next to you for at least one full set.

social.title: Craft Cocktails at Williams & Graham in the Highlands
social.description: This speakeasy disguised as a bookshop has set Denver's cocktail standard for over a decade — pull the right book, slip inside, and let bartenders who treat every drink like a thesis take over.
social.bonus: Tell the bartender your mood, not your order — accept whatever they make without asking what's in it.

social.title: Denver Nuggets Game at Ball Arena
social.description: Watching Nikola Jokić orchestrate a half-court offense live at Ball Arena is a basketball education that no highlight reel properly prepares you for.
social.bonus: Buy a standing room ticket, find the loudest section, and stay on your feet for the entire fourth quarter.

social.title: First Friday Art Walk in the RiNo Art District
social.description: On the first Friday of every month, River North's galleries, studios, and warehouses open their doors simultaneously and the neighborhood turns into a walkable party that's half gallery show, half block party.
social.bonus: Walk into one gallery where you understand nothing — ask the artist or staff to explain one piece in the room.

social.title: Live Music at the Bluebird Theater
social.description: The Bluebird has been putting acts into Denver's Colfax Ave corridor since 1913 — the 550-person standing room format makes it one of the best rooms in the country to see a band before they're too big for it.
social.bonus: Buy a drink for the person next to you and find out why they're here for this specific artist.

social.title: Rockies Game at Coors Field
social.description: Grab a seat in the outfield and settle in for nine innings under the Denver sky.
social.bonus: Catch a foul ball — or at least try.

chill.title: Get Lost in the Tattered Cover on Colfax
chill.description: Denver's great independent bookstore fills a converted theater on East Colfax with worn armchairs and staff picks that actually mean something — an institution the city refused to let die.
chill.bonus: Read the first chapter of something in an armchair before deciding — that's what they're for.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Clyfford Still Museum
chill.description: This intimate museum on Bannock holds 94% of Still's entire lifetime output — one of the most complete single-artist collections anywhere — in rooms so quiet you can hear yourself think.
chill.bonus: Pick one painting and stand in front of it for ten uninterrupted minutes — no reading the placard first.

chill.title: Late Afternoon at the Denver Museum of Nature and Science
chill.description: This grand civic institution in City Park has anchored Denver's cultural life since 1900 — its gem and mineral hall alone justifies the entire afternoon.
chill.bonus: Find the largest single gemstone in the mineral hall and spend five full minutes with it — no phone.

chill.title: Afternoon Beer at Great Divide Brewing on Arapahoe
chill.description: One of Denver's founding craft breweries since 1994, Great Divide's taproom pours Yeti Imperial Stout year-round in a no-frills warehouse that never pretended to be a trendy beer garden.
chill.bonus: Order the Yeti on nitro if it's available, then work through at least two more styles you've never tried before leaving.

chill.title: Vinyl Dig at Wax Trax Records on East Colfax
chill.description: Denver's legendary punk and metal record shop has survived since 1975 on East Colfax because the bins are genuinely deep and the staff will either make your day or ruin your budget.
chill.bonus: Set a $30 limit, go straight to the used bins, and leave with something you've never heard of — no Shazam allowed.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Molly Brown House Museum
chill.description: The Victorian Capitol Hill mansion of the original Unsinkable Molly Brown is as wild and over-decorated as the woman herself — one of Denver's best preserved glimpses into Gilded Age excess.
chill.bonus: Ask your guide the one thing about Brown that the Titanic movie got completely wrong.

chill.title: Sunset Walk on the 16th Street Mall
chill.description: The mile-long pedestrian corridor looks its best at golden hour when the old Daniels & Fisher Tower glows and the free shuttle hums past buskers still earning their keep.
chill.bonus: Stop and actually listen to one busker for at least three full songs before moving on — leave a real tip.

chill.title: Espresso and a Book at Novo Coffee on Sherman
chill.description: Denver's most serious independent roaster since 2002 pulls a single origin espresso that makes it genuinely hard to leave the light-flooded Sherman Street café.
chill.bonus: Order black, whatever they're featuring on the espresso bar today — no milk, no syrup, just taste the thing.

chill.title: Wander the Denver Botanic Gardens
chill.description: Twenty-four acres of curated plant collections in the middle of the city, at their most surreal during the winter when the cactus house is the warmest room in Colorado.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest plant specimen on the grounds — ask a staff member, not Google — and sit with it for five minutes.

chill.title: Afternoon in Washington Park
chill.description: Denver's great lawn — two lakes, a boat house, giant elms, and a 2.6-mile loop where the whole city seems to exhale every Sunday afternoon.
chill.bonus: Rent a paddleboat on Grasmere Lake and stay out until the ranger waves you back in.

chill.title: Read the Afternoon Away at Cheesman Park
chill.description: Cheesman Park's formal pavilion and wide lawns occupy one of Denver's most beautiful residential neighborhoods, where old-growth elms shade a park that's been a city anchor since 1898.
chill.bonus: Leave a book you loved on a bench with a handwritten note inside the cover for whoever finds it.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Denver Art Museum
chill.description: The DAM's collection of Native American art is one of the finest in the country, and Daniel Libeskind's titanium-paneled Frederic C. Hamilton Building is worth entering just to stand inside the geometry.
chill.bonus: Find the piece in the Native Arts collection that stops you cold — sit in front of it for five full minutes without moving on.
